tasha: Heads up — onboarding sample app on Android 13 is producing doubled uploads after a flaky cellular->wifi handoff. Two POSTs for the same file. quick repro steps in gist: cold start, flip network, trigger upload.

benji: Are you seeing two separate network calls or one retry? OkHttp can replay requests on authenticator retry paths if body is not repeatable.

tasha: Two separate calls. Logs show token refresh started twice around the same ms. We're currently using a suspend refresh in an Interceptor.

lee: Interceptor+suspend = risky. Interceptors are synchronous wrt OkHttp threads; suspend may switch dispatchers causing races. Authenticator or a dedicated token provider is safer.

benji: Also check whether request body is a non-repeatable stream. If body isn't buffered, OkHttp may not be able to replay; but in your case server got two distinct requests.

lee: Fixes we've used: 1) move to Authenticator for 401 flows; 2) central TokenManager exposing a single-flight Deferred or Mutex; 3) server-side idempotency keys.

tasha: Any sample code for the single-flight Deferred approach?

benji: Quick sketch: "val currentRefresh = AtomicReference<Deferred<Token>?>(null)" then CAS to set a new async refresh when null, else await existing. Works across coroutines and avoids synchronized pitfalls.

build-bot: Created PR 3482: adds devex/samples/token-singleflight-atomic.kt and updates docs/devex/auth.md

tasha: Awesome — I'll try the Atomic Deferred approach and swap the Interceptor for an Authenticator. Will report back. Thanks!
